intelligence.enrichment: The Indian National Calendar is a solar calendar with 365 days in a year, used by the Government of India along with the Gregorian calendar, and its year begins on 22 March, the day after the spring equinox. Official calendar design follows the solar year -> a 365-day solar calendar is used alongside the Gregorian calendar -> the year starts just after the spring equinox. The learner correctly applies this rule: The Indian National Calendar is a solar calendar with 365 days in a year, used by the Government of India along with the Gregorian calendar, and its year begins on 22 March, the day after the spring equinox. India only uses the Gregorian calendar for official dates, so the Indian National Calendar is not a solar official calendar.
